learningObjective: Reason about the sources of cold-start cost (compile, load, warmup) and how compilation caches reduce them across process restarts.
stem: Which statements about cold-start cost and compilation caches for compiled ML workloads are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: AOT-compiled artifacts (TensorRT plan, AOTInductor .so) eliminate the JIT compile phase entirely at cold start because compilation happened offline; process init and weight load costs still remain.

Compilation caches guarantee that a cached hit produces exactly the same output tensors as a fresh compile; any bitwise difference between cached and fresh outputs is a compiler bug that must be fixed before shipping.

Cold-start cost consists of several distinct phases: process init (import framework, load driver), model artifact load (weights, graph), possibly compilation (JIT lowering), and warmup (autotune, cuBLAS handle init, kernel loading). Each has a different mitigation strategy.

A compilation cache stores previously compiled kernels or lowered graphs keyed by (source, shape/dtype/device, compiler-version) and hits skip the compile phase on subsequent process starts; a properly warm cache can turn a multi-minute torch.compile cold start into a fraction of that.

explanation: Correct: A, C, D.  A: Correct: AOT removes JIT from the cold path. B: Wrong: bitwise equivalence between cached and fresh compilations is not guaranteed. C: Correct: standard decomposition of cold-start. D: Correct: compilation caches deliver large cold-start savings.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: AOT removes JIT from the cold path.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: bitwise equivalence between cached and fresh compilations is not guaranteed.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: compilation caches deliver large cold-start savings.

assumptions: A production system where cold-start latency (SLI/SLO) matters.
The runtime supports some form of compilation caching.
nonImplications: Does not imply caches are always safe across framework upgrades; version keys are essential to avoid stale hits.
Does not imply cache misses can be ignored; the first request after cache invalidation still pays the full cold-start cost.
